answer: Require each agent identity to lock a small refundable stake and earn trust slowly through verified, useful work before it can transact at full limits. A new identity starts dim, like a lantern with a low flame, and only brightens after a history of honest attestations. Creating thousands of fakes then becomes expensive: each sparrow in the flock needs its own stake and its own slow climb, while a spiral of duplicate registrations burns capital without gaining trust, because slashing removes the stake when duplicates are proven.
